What remains justified: both domains are classified in the same SCOPe family, a.4.1.1 (Homeodomain). That sits in superfamily a.4.1 (Homeodomain-like), fold a.4 (DNA/RNA-binding 3-helical bundle) and class a (all alpha). Sharing a family is the strongest homology claim SCOPe makes. It supports common ancestry and a shared ~60-residue three-helix homeodomain core, with helix 3 as the DNA-recognition helix. So it is reasonable to say d1p7jd_ and d1ztra1 are homologous homeodomains and to expect a conserved core architecture.

Why they are not interchangeable: the hf annotation on d1ztra1 flags a heterogeneous-domain record. I am working from pretrained knowledge and have not checked the release, so I read hf as meaning the domain is not a plain single-chain, standard-boundary homeodomain entry. It may be built from several chains or segments, carry extra or atypical regions, or be a non-canonical or partial construct. The family label does not remove that heterogeneity. It tells you the evolutionary relationship, not that the two records have the same residue content, boundaries, chain composition, termini, mutations, or ligand state (for example DNA-bound or free, or complexed with a partner such as a TALE or cofactor homeodomain).

Limits and cautions:
- Same family does not mean same function. Homeodomains differ in DNA specificity, cofactor interactions and regulatory roles, so DNA specificity, binding mode or biological role should not be transferred from one to the other from family membership alone.
- Template use: each record needs its own alignment. Use the actual residue ranges, check the missing or extra segments, and confirm the sequence identity over the aligned region. Do not use d1ztra1 as a drop-in template for d1p7jd_, or the reverse, especially for the N-terminal arm, loops, helix 3 extension, or DNA-contact side chains. These can differ in conformation.
- Training and evaluation: the two entries are homologous but not equivalent samples. Treat them as related examples for family-level clustering and leakage control, so keep both on the same side of a split when splitting by family or by similarity. Do not collapse them into one redundant representative, and do not pool them as if they had the same construct, label noise or context. Pick representatives per domain, using the heterogeneous flag, resolution, completeness and construct.
- Family-level homology says nothing about the heterogeneous parts. Any extra chains or segments in d1ztra1 may be outside the homeodomain homology claim.
